stanza: Shows there's money to be made
That's the history of the trade
Did you add up all the cards

gamble.line: But me, I'm not a gamble
stanza: And I know you have a heavy heart
I can feel it when we kiss
So many men stronger than me
Have thrown their backs out trying to lift it
But me, I'm not a gamble
You can count on me to split
The love I sell you in the evening

ramble.line: In Yorkshire near Rotherham, he had been on the ramble
stanza: In Yorkshire near Rotherham, he had been on the ramble
Weary of travelling, he sat down to rest
By the foot of yon' mountain
With bread and cold water he himself did refresh
